outcomes: A task's observations reach the CLI and Putnami Cloud as data the cache keeps, never as a task of their own
One reader decides what a fragment file says, so the producer, the CLI and Delivery cannot disagree about it
nonGoals: Deciding a verdict: a fragment states a fact, and the reader that applies a policy decides
The fragment kinds other than finding, which later versions of this feature add

text: A fragment file holds one JSON object per line, each of protocolVersion 1 and of a closed kind, finding in this version.
A line that is blank, not an object, of another version or kind, or that holds an undeclared member or a member of the wrong type fails, naming its line.
A finding carries source.format, subject.path, a clean slash path relative to the task's project that never leaves it, and optionally subject.symbol, subject.line and subject.column.
It names its rule, a severity of error, warning or info, and a message; it states no project, task or verdict.
A fragment file holds at most 50000 fragments and 16 MiB; a string is at most 4 KiB.
A file over a bound fails as a whole.
The reserved artifact identity putnami-evidence names the file putnami-evidence.jsonl in a task's command output, so a cache hit that restores the file restores the artifact.
